title: Bypassing Skip-Gram Negative Sampling: Dimension Regularization as a More Efficient Alternative for Graph Embeddings

problem.claim: Graph embedding objectives need repulsion to prevent embeddings from collapsing into trivial solutions.

gap.claim: SGNS provides node-wise repulsion, but a more scalable alternative based on dimension operations is needed.

contributions.claim: The work establishes that, near collapse, aggregate SGNS node-wise repulsion approximately re-centers embedding dimensions.
The work proposes dimension regularization as an efficient alternative to SGNS and a flexible augmentation framework for algorithms using SGNS.
For LINE and node2vec, the augmented algorithms preserve downstream link-prediction performance while reducing GPU memory usage and training time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: For LINE and node2vec, the framework reportedly reduces GPU memory usage by up to 33.3% and training time by 23.4% while preserving link-prediction performance.
Removing repulsion in LINE reportedly reduces training time by 70.9% on average and increases link-prediction performance, especially on globally sparse but locally dense graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph embedding objectives combine attraction and repulsion, with repulsion preventing collapse.
SGNS prevents collapse through node-wise repulsion from sampled dissimilar nodes.
Near collapse, aggregate SGNS repulsion approximately re-centers embedding dimensions, motivating dimension regularization.
The authors propose replacing SGNS with dimension regularization through a generic augmentation framework.
Experiments with LINE and node2vec report preserved link-prediction performance and lower resource use, with stronger effects for removing repulsion in selected graph structures.

source_observation.claim: When node-wise repulsion is approximately equivalent to dimension re-centering near collapse, dimension-level operations can replace node-level operations.

interpretation.claim: An optimization expressed over dimensions may offer better scalability and simpler geometry than an equivalent operation over nodes.

application.claim: For embedding objectives with attraction and repulsion, investigate dimension regularization as a replacement or augmentation for sampled negative-node contrast.

exception.claim: Repulsion is generally still needed; removing it is reported as beneficial particularly for globally sparse but locally dense graphs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact dimension-regularization operation.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, statistical variation, or experimental protocols.
